messages:
Maria Chen: Quick design scrub — posted two prototypes for the Settings form error UX. Prototype A = inline-first (field-level copy + red border). Prototype B = lightweight inline hints + top summary/toast after submit. Also included a separate flow for bulk destructive actions. Looking for accessibility, copy, and mobile density takeaways. Devin Patel: skimmed both — my 2¢: inline errors are clearer for single-field edits, summary is nice for long forms. worry: toast burying errors on mobile. Samir K.: Agree with Devin. Also — inline-only can be noisy on dense admin tables. For bulk ops we need both: per-row inline and a top-level summary when many rows fail. Rika Sato: Accessibility nit: if using a top summary, we must announce it to screen readers (aria-live) and move focus to it after submit failure. Example suggestion for an assertive region: ```
You have 3 errors. Fix the highlighted fields or expand the summary.
``` Maria Chen: good call on focus. For the summary copy I'm leaning to: "Save failed — 3 problems need attention. Review the list or fix fields inline." Thoughts on tone? Devin Patel: that's fine. Maybe shorten to: "Save failed — 3 issues. See details below." We want scannable. Also, highlight the first error in the DOM and focus it for keyboard users. Samir K.: Required marker debate: current proposal uses asterisk only. Accessibility research suggests asterisk alone isn't reliably discoverable for some users. Option A: visible "Required" helper text under label; Option B: use `aria-required` + tooltip for sighted users. I prefer showing the word "Required" for critical forms. Rika Sato: +1 for explicit "Required" label in dense admin forms. Asterisk can be retained visually, but the text reduces ambiguity. For mobile we can hide the word if space constrained but ensure `aria-required` remains. Maria Chen: copy tweak suggestion for required hint: label: "Account name" and helper: "Required — used for billing and URLs." Short and actionable. Devin Patel: destructive confirmation options for bulk delete — we prototyped three: 1) modal with typed-confirm (`Type DELETE`), 2) modal with exact-name typing, 3) snackbar undo. For true irreversible deletes we should prefer typed-confirm or exact-name. For soft deletes, snackbar undo + quick recover is better. Samir K.: typed-confirm is good for power users but slows down support workflows. Maybe use exact-name for org-level deletes, typed-confirm for dataset/table-level irreversible actions, and prompt to use undo for daily bulk operations. Rika Sato: accessibility for typed-confirm: ensure the input has an accessible label and that screen readers can announce the required pattern. Also provide a keyboard-only flow that doesn't rely on drag/drop or mouse. Maria Chen: UXBot run: DesignBot ran an a11y check on both prototypes — summary plus inline got flagged for missing focus transfer and low contrast on the inline helper text. DesignBot: Quick scan results: color contrast for helper text in Prototype A is 3.8:1 (fail). `aria-live` region missing explicit label in Prototype B (recommend: provide `aria-label=\"Form errors\"`). Devin Patel: ok actionable items: 1) enforce contrast >= 4.5:1 for inline helper text OR increase weight; 2) implement focus transfer to summary on submit fail; 3) prefer explicit "Required" label for dense forms; 4) adopt typed-confirm only for irreversible org-level deletes, add snackbar undo for bulk soft-deletes. Maria Chen: love it. I'll make a small PR with copy updates and a11y tweaks and post the updated prototypes. Thanks everyone — tagging @Samir for follow-up on the exact-name modal wording. :slightly_smiling_face:
